ledger.claim: The fare breakdown fixes the economics of this trip: it is an UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 27.90, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were settled at booking and no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs. What the rider can be made to bear beyond the quote is confined to the pass-through and statutory lines POL-RD-09 makes properly chargeable, and to nothing else.

On the platform's own ledger the airport_surcharge line is 0.00 and the total_charged of 27.90 equals quoted_fare_sgd of 27.90 exactly, with charged_over_quote at 0.00. No line of the fare breakdown raises any airport surcharge at all, so the SGD 40 the driver demanded off-app answers to no charge the platform ever billed.

The chat log records the driver's own words, 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls'. That representation is contradicted by the platform's fare model, which carries a structured airport surcharge for trips originating at Changi (SGD 6.00 off-peak, SGD 8.00 peak), and by the fare breakdown itself, which has an airport_surcharge field. The app does handle an airport surcharge; the premise on which the off-app payment was demanded is false.

The trip record gives the pickup as 'Changi Airport Terminal 2, Arrival Pick-up Door 3', so this trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport and any airport surcharge is chargeable in principle. But the most that could ever be properly chargeable on it is the fare model's SGD 6.00/8.00 line, so the SGD 40 collected bears no relation to any lawful surcharge and cannot be a fare component.

Because the only airport surcharge the policy permits on this trip is the fare model's SGD 6.00/8.00 line and the ledger bills 0.00, the SGD 40 taken off-app under the label 'airport surcharge' is a surcharge wrongly applied within POL-RD-11(b). It is a pass-through correction under POL-RD-09, not a distance or time charge, and POL-RD-11's bar on distance refunds therefore does not reach it. The rider should not carry an off-tariff surcharge the fare record does not contain.

I concede the route point honestly: the GPS trace is complete (100% coverage, 133 fixes, no gaps, admissibility weight 1.0) and records a trace distance of 15.79 km against a booked optimal of 15.5 km, an excess of 0.29 km and 1.87%, below both POL-RD-01 thresholds of 0.8 km and 20%. No route deviation is established and the rider does not press a distance-based refund; the complaint is the off-tariff payment, not the road driven.

The driver's answer that the payment 'was voluntary' does not meet the point. The chat log shows the demand was framed as a platform requirement ('cannot in app'), and neither POL-RD-09 nor POL-RD-11 channels any fare component through a private payment; consent obtained on a representation the fare record contradicts cannot convert an unbilled surcharge into a properly chargeable line.

The rider's own history carries no corroboration uplift: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration factor for sub-30% claims is not engaged, and no other field on the rider profile may be used to discount this claim because POL-GEN-01 makes every remaining profile field context only.

If the tribunal concludes that the off-tariff sum cannot be resolved inside the fare arithmetic, the disputed amount should be held and not collected: under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it, and on a rider-filed dispute that is the only outcome that stops the rider funding a surcharge the fare record does not carry.

The POL-RD-01 threshold test is measured on the trace, not on the rounded trip record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 15.79 km against a booked optimal of 15.5 km, an excess of 0.29 km — 1.87% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20% of optimal_distance_km; it exceeds neither. No route deviation is therefore established on this trip, and the rider's route claim fails at the gate however she characterises the trip.

The fare is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: quoted_fare_sgd is 27.90 and charged_total is 27.90. Under POL-RD-11, POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted trip and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess would be. The only POL-RD-11 remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quoted fare plus the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines — 27.90 less 27.90 — and the ledger's own computation of that remedy is 0.00.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace is entirely unimpaired and yields an excess of 0.29 km, so limb (b) of that burden is not discharged. The burden never shifts to the driver, and the rider's own numerical case fails without the driver needing to invoke any exculpatory clause at all.

There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09(4): the ledger carries no ERP gantry lines and no tolls, and airport_surcharge is 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge on this trip. The trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 2, so an airport surcharge is a properly chargeable pass-through under POL-RD-09 which the platform simply did not bill — which is precisely why the driver's account that the app did not cover the airport cost has a basis in the fare model rather than being an invented charge.

The trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes: 133 fixes at a 10 second cadence, coverage_pct of 100.0, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds. The case therefore does not engage the POL-RD-10(3) impairment escalation, nor the POL-RD-10(5) route, and the record is sufficient for a final monetary ruling rather than an escalation.

POL-RD-06 is not engaged. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250 — a ratio of 0.00, below both the 3-flag test and the 0.05-ratio test with at least 40 completed trips. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) applies and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arises on this record.

What the rider has formally contested is the in-app charge of SGD 27.90, which is exactly the quoted fare, and the PayNow transfer she narrates is not a line of the fare_breakdown at all — it is not a distance, time, ERP, toll or surcharge line that POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-09 can correct. The rider's own chat reply 'ok sent' confirms she was told the reason and the amount before she paid. The rider's claim is not supported by the fare record, and on NO_ACTION the present payment state — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — simply stands.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the ride and the in-app fare are clean, and nothing on the platform ledger changes. Rider, your route-deviation point fails: the GPS trace measures 15.79 km against the booked optimal of 15.5 km — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87% — and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km and 20%. Your own advocate conceded this. With no deviation established, no distance refund arises, and because the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE (quoted fare SGD 27.90), POL-RD-11 closes the distance-refund route in any event. The in-app charge of SGD 27.90 equals the quoted fare exactly (charged_over_quote 0.00), and the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and an airport_surcharge of 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge on the ledger for POL-RD-09 to correct.

The SGD 40 you sent by PayNow is a real grievance but a different thing from a fare line. POL-RD-09 and POL-RD-11 correct only charges the platform billed, and the platform never billed that sum — it appears nowhere in the fare breakdown. Your advocate's argument that it is a 'surcharge wrongly applied' under POL-RD-11(b) cannot succeed: POL-RD-09(4) treats an airport surcharge as wrongly applied only on a trip that does not ORIGINATE at an airport, and this trip started at Changi Airport Terminal 2, where a surcharge is properly chargeable in principle; and in any event no surcharge was actually charged (the line is 0.00). I do record that the driver's premise was false: the fare model does carry a structured Changi surcharge (SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak), so telling you the app 'cannot' handle it was contradicted by the platform's own rate card, and an off-tariff SGD 40 bears no relation to the SGD 6.00/8.00 line. But that is an open question between you and the driver, not something a clause in this policy lets the platform move, and I note it as such rather than as a referral.

Rider, your request for an ESCALATE holding the disputed amount is refused. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires: the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 133 fixes, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), the trip identifiers all match, the timestamps agree, no refund exceeds any ceiling, and no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00531-01, weight 0.0) is not relied on by anyone — neither side asserts an external traffic cause, so the missing advisory decides nothing here.

Driver, your account that the payment was voluntary does not convert the SGD 40 into a fare component, and the off-app sum cannot be refunded through the fare system either; the consequence is simply that the in-app fare stands. I have not used either profile against either party (POL-GEN-01), and no clause produces a conduct or billing-integrity referral on this record.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The fare_breakdown stands as it is — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, charged_total SGD 27.90.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
